transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Maud 3 FP, Hask 3 FP, Eira 3 FP, Fenwick 3 FP. Face-up: Endless Rain [H-01], The Wick Lane Cellars [L-05].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Rain drums on the shingled roof of the Ropewalk, Hollowmoot's driest tavern, and drips through it anyway in three places the barkeep has given up bailing. The town outside is a maze of swaying walkways and lashed pilings, lantern-light smeared gold in the downpour, quarantine bells tolling faint and far off toward the temple. At a back table a cartel fixer waits with watered gin and a ledger, tapping a column of names — some of them yours — and says the cellars under Wick Lane have gone silent a day early, which never happens. Someone needs to go down and find out why, and the fixer's smile makes clear that "someone" isn't a request.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: The cellars go quiet sometimes. So before I wade into flooded smuggler warrens on your say-so, I want to know what changed—rain, missed reports, or something new moving in? And if I'm risking it, you tell me straight what you're really looking for.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud leans back and meets Tallow's eyes directly, refusing to be rattled by the implicit threat. She probes for real information about what happened in the cellars, making clear she knows the work is dangerous and wants to understand it before committing. She acknowledges the debt without flinching.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: I'll go down to the cellars. I know the dark and the damp better than most, and if something's wrong, I'll find it before it finds any of you.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask straightens from his seat, leaving his cup untouched. He steps forward into the lamplight, meeting Tallow's eyes directly with the steady gaze of someone who knows the drowned places beneath murky water. His weathered hand rests naturally at his side, familiar with danger.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: My name's on that page, Tallow—you want to tell me why before you start making demands? And these cellars have gone quiet before. What's different this time?

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira sets down her drink and leans forward, her eyes steady on Tallow's, jaw tight. She doesn't look away from that ledger—she looks like she's reading every name on it, and she's not impressed by the implied threat.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: The silence troubles you more than most things. What happened down there—or what *didn't* happen—that's got you concerned enough to pull in markers?

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick approaches Tallow's table without apparent hesitation and sits across from the fixer, keeping his posture loose but attentive. He glances briefly at the ledger before meeting Tallow's eyes.)

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: A bigger cut changes the math. I'm in.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Maud accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Tallow's smile widens as the coin gets mentioned; he slides a chip across the table to Maud without breaking eye contact with the others. "Bigger cut, sure. But you'll want to know this too—" he taps the ledger once, "the last report from Wick Lane mentioned singing. Not the swarm-song from the temple bells, something else, closer, under the floorboards. My man down there didn't finish his sentence before the message stopped." He shrugs, like it's nothing, but his knuckles are white on the ledger's spine. Word of the job reaches Sister Orla before you've even left the Ropewalk—she corners Maud on the stilt-walk outside, rain streaming off her hood, insisting this is a sign from the Dry Saint and that Maud must carry a relic candle down into the dark "to see what answers the light." Maud, this is dangerous and slows you down, but Orla won't be told no easily. Hask, Eira and Fenwick fall in as you make for Wick Lane, the rain swallowing your footsteps and the town's lantern-glow fading behind you into the endless grey wet.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: You take the back stair off Wick Lane, the one with the loose board that only cartel feet know to skip, down into a warren of low brick arches and stacked crates wrapped against the wet. Lantern light catches sacking, salt-barrels, the glint of a smuggler's hatch bolted into the floor above black water. And beneath it all, faint, wrong, threading up through the damp stone — a sound like singing, too even to be human, too close to be the temple bells. Dry goods here mean someone's kept this place sealed against the rain for a reason; the question is whether that reason still wants visitors.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: Hold—do you hear that? It's not the temple bells, and it's no voice I know. Everyone stay sharp and watch the water.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud raises her fist in a sharp halt signal, her militia training kicking in automatic. She moves slowly toward the hatch with one hand resting on her weapon, staying in shadow between the crate-stacks. Eyes scanning the black water and sealed goods, she gestures for the others to spread out and keep alert—this is no abandoned cellar, and that singing means something still guards it.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: That's no swarm-song and it's no drowned bell—it's something *else* down there, something kept.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask crouches by the bolted hatch and traces the singing to its source, letting his marsh-hunter senses map the sound through stone and water. He moves carefully toward where the noise is strongest, staying low, watching for signs of what might be singing beneath the floorboards.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: I know every sound the swamp makes, and that isn't one of them. Show yourself.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira strides toward the singing, her swamp-born ear tracking it beneath the sealed floorboards. She runs her fingers over cold stone, feeling for vibrations—this is no natural sound, too perfect, too measured for anything that lives and breathes in the Sallowmere.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: That's not the swarm-song from the temple—that's something underneath, something orchestrated. We need to know what's keeping these goods dry before we go lower.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick moves deeper into the cellar warren, staying low and keeping one hand on the damp brick wall. He traces the singing—that too-even, too-wrong sound—trying to pinpoint its source beneath the arches. His mind flips through old surveying notes, Bren's old codes, checking them against what he knows of these passages and how they connect downward.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: Blast these stones—the walls are closing in, I can't breathe!

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Hask — overcome with Notice: dice 0 - - + → Good (+3) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira — overcome with Lore: dice + + - 0, invoking Knows the old plague wards by heart [EI-01] → Fantastic (+6) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: {"narration":"Eira presses flat against the stone, fighting down the closing-walls panic even as she uses it — the old plague-ward chants come back to her fingers before her mind catches up, and she realizes the wrongness of the sound isn't magic, it's rhythm: someone down there is counting, in the same cadence the quarantine wardens once used to mark hours in the sealed houses. Hask, low by the hatch, feels the vibration change tempo the moment Eira's hand finds the right stone — whatever's singing knows it's been heard. Between them they trace the sound past the hatch, down through a narrower seam in the brick that isn't on any smuggler's map Fenwick recognizes, and it's there, half-buried in old crate-manifests wedged in the seam, that Eira's fingers close on a scrap of paper in a hand she knows too well: Sella's. A name, a date, a tally of coin — the Warden's informer has been down here before, and recently. The singing doesn't stop. It just waits, closer now, patient as the rain."}

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: That's Sella's script—the Warden's informant. She's been making coin down here, and recent. Whatever's singing, it's not frenzied. It's watching us like we're watching it. Nobody moves until we know what we're facing. Hask, Eira—is there more on that paper?

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud steps forward to examine the scrap with Sella's handwriting, her militia bearing straightening immediately. She traces the hatch with her eyes, reading positions and sightlines—the singing, the black water, the sealed goods, the path back. Her jaw sets. She turns to her companions with a sharp gesture: hold the line, stay spread, watch the water. Her hand rests on her weapon but stays sheathed. She's held a position before; you don't rush blind into occupied ground.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Something's keeping watch in this place. I'm getting closer—all of you hold position and don't follow until I signal.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask moves low through the shadows between crate-stacks toward the bolted hatch, keeping his weight light on the wet stone. He traces the singing's vibration through the damp brick, moving silent as marsh-mist, trying to close the distance and get close enough to assess what's waiting in the dark below before it can move against them.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: Sella's been here, and she's wrapped up in this. I'm going down there and I'm going to know why.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira holds up the paper bearing Sella's handwriting, her jaw clenched hard enough to ache. That hand—she'd know it anywhere. Sella, who sold out her family to save herself. Without hesitation, Eira shoulders into the narrow seam in the brick, moving quietly but urgently through the cramped passage toward the source of that patient, waiting singing. The tight space makes her breath catch—walls closing in—but she pushes through it, driven by anger and the burning need for answers about what Sella's been doing down here.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: That cadence—it's the old quarantine count. Whoever's singing, they're keeping time like a warden sealing a house. And if Sella knew this place, we need to know what she was counting toward.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick kneels beside Eira and examines Sella's note carefully, cycling through the quarantine ward cadences he learned from old survey records. The rhythm threading up through the stone matches exactly—it's the Warden's count, the measure used to mark sealed plague houses year after year. Someone down there is keeping deliberate time, marking something important. Sella knew this place. The Wardens' watch runs deeper than anyone thought.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Hask — overcome with Stealth: dice + 0 0 - → Good (+3) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira — overcome with Stealth: dice - - + +, invoking Owed a truth Sella will never give freely [EI-02] → Great (+4) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Fenwick — create advantage with Lore: dice + 0 - -, invoking Can still read Brens old notes and codes [FE-02] → Superb (+5) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Hask reaches the hatch's far side first, flattening into a niche where the brick opens onto a low chamber half-lit by a single shielded lantern — and goes stone-still, signaling back with two fingers: wait, look. Eira pushes through the narrow seam behind him, breath ragged from the tight stone, and gets her answer whether she wanted it now or not: chained to an iron ring bolted into the crypt-wet floor is a hive-touched man, rocking, counting the old quarantine cadence under his breath like a hymn — and beside him, tallow candles arranged with careful, recent precision, is a second scrap in Sella's hand: a tally of dates matching every Warden bell-toll for the last month. Fenwick, kneeling over the first note, puts it together aloud before anyone can stop him — Sella isn't just informing on the cartel to the Wardens, she's been timing something down here, feeding someone's captivity to match the town's quarantine bells exactly, and whoever she answers to wanted it kept quiet enough to bury under Wick Lane. The singing man's head snaps up at the sound of Fenwick's voice, milky eyes finding the lantern-light, and from somewhere above and behind them — up the stair they came down — heavy boots start moving with purpose. Someone up top just realized visitors let themselves in.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: I know your name. I know hers. And I know what you're asking of me — so stop begging and show me where she's gone.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Maud accepts the compel on 'Hollowmoot's Faithful'.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The shielded lantern doesn't just light empty stone — it catches a woman huddled against the far wall, soaked to the bone, rocking in time with the counting-song like it's a hymn she can't stop singing back. Hask knows a civilian panic-freeze when he sees one and holds Eira back with a flat hand. Then the lantern-light catches her face properly, and Maud, crowding in behind them both, goes cold: it's Yara Bell, whose boy drowned at the Ashwater crossing last spring, whose grief Maud sat with for three nights running. Yara shouldn't be within a mile of Wick Lane. But here she is, ankle-deep in the flood, mouthing the same three notes over and over, staring at the black water like it owes her something back.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: Yara, it's me. I know what you lost. I sat with you those three nights. Come back to me—come back now.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud wades through the black water toward Yara, reaching out with steady hands. She moves like someone who knows this grief intimately—who has mourned alongside it, who carries the weight of knowing every family's secret sorrow in Hollowmoot.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Yara, look at me. Come on—take my hand and let's get you out of this water.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask holds Eira back with a flat hand, then steps forward slowly with open palms. He positions himself between Yara and the black water, movement deliberate and careful. He recognizes the look of someone left behind, lost in their grief.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: Yara, I know that song—I know the wardens taught us those words. What are you doing down here in the black water?

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira pushes past Hask's restraining hand and moves forward into the lamp-light. Her breath is still ragged from the tight passages, but recognizing the plague ward rhythm—the old cadence she learned as a child behind the quarantine fence—her voice steadies. She approaches Yara slowly and carefully, the way she's learned to move toward people gripped by panic or deep grief.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: That's not her singing—that's something singing *through* her. The rhythm matches Bren's last recordings, before the hive took him. She's being pulled toward something in that water.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick steps into the lantern-light beside Hask and Eira, listening intently to Yara's counting-song. His mind catches the familiar pulse from Bren's fevered notes—the telltale structure of hive-influence. He traces the pattern in the air, recognizing not random panic but a deliberate summons threading beneath every note.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Maud — overcome with Empathy: dice - 0 - + → Fair (+2) vs Terrible (-2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Hask — overcome with Empathy: dice 0 - + 0 → Fair (+2) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Fenwick — create advantage with Lore: dice 0 - + 0 → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Maud doesn't fight the water so much as walk through it like she's done it a hundred times at a hundred bedsides — she reaches Yara, gets both hands on her shoulders, and speaks the names of Yara's own dead son until the counting cracks and breaks into a sob instead. Hask keeps his body between the two women and the black hatch-water the whole time, a wall of calm that gives Yara somewhere safe to fall apart. Fenwick, tracing the rhythm in the air, feels it click into place against Bren's old fevered notebooks: this isn't grief and it isn't madness, it's a summons, deliberate and patterned, pulling anyone attuned enough toward Saint Orrin's belltower — and now that Fenwick's named the shape of it, the whole party can feel the pull too, faint but constant, like a fishhook set behind the sternum. Yara comes back to herself enough to gasp out fragments: she followed the singing down here three nights running, sure it was her boy calling her from the water. It wasn't. Something else knows exactly what voice to borrow.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Yara's sobbing breaks into ragged words between gasps — she isn't just hive-touched-adjacent, she's been a lookout, planted by someone to listen for a rhythm in the water and count it back. Maud keeps her grounded with a hand on her shoulder while Hask watches the hatch, certain now that whoever set her here will notice the singing stopped. Upstairs, floorboards creak with weight that isn't rain-swell — booted feet, moving with purpose toward the cellar stair. The party has a handful of minutes to get what they need from Yara before the Wick Lane Cellars decide who else gets to hear it.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: Who sent you? Who made you count? I need the name, Yara, and I need it right now.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud steps into the narrow space beside Yara like she's locking into a shield-wall—solid, immovable, present. She grips both of Yara's shoulders and meets her eyes with the full weight of Hollowmoot's trust. 'Who set you here? Who made you count? Give me the name right now—give me what I need and I hold the line with you, Yara. Who is it?')

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Keep her talking, Maud. I'll meet them at the door.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask rises smoothly from his guard position, moving with marsh-learned silence toward the cellar stair entrance. He positions himself in the shadows where the stairs open into the low chamber—not blocking it, but set to intercept whoever comes down before their eyes adjust and they see the others.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: I'll meet them on the stairs. You two get what you need from her—fast.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira moves fast to the cellar stairs, sinking into the shadows at the lowest step where the lantern light doesn't reach. She settles into the stone, shoulders loose, ready. When the enforcer comes down they'll see her first—and stepping into *her* ground will cost them something.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: Yara—listen to me. Who put you here? What were you counting?

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick closes the distance as Maud steadies Yara, his mind already mapping the threads—the song, the pattern, the hive. The footsteps on the cellar stairs grow louder. He crouches to eye level with Yara, voice urgent but level.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Maud — create advantage with Rapport: dice - - - 0 → Average (+1) vs Mediocre (+0): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Hask — overcome with Stealth: dice - 0 - +, invoking Moves silent as marsh-mist to reach the lost [HA-03] → Great (+4) vs Great (+4): TIE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira — create advantage with Stealth: dice + + - -, invoking Born in the Hollowmoot quarantine house [EI-01], Knows the old plague wards by heart [EI-01] → Fantastic (+6) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Fenwick — overcome with Investigate: dice + + + + → Epic (+7) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: As Hask slips into position at the stair-mouth, somewhere above and out toward the market the quarantine bells start tolling — Hollowmoot's watchtower has caught wind of trouble, and now every Warden ear in earshot knows something's wrong on Wick Lane. Hask still gets his ambush position at the door, but the enforcer coming down isn't alone in being alerted: the whole street above is stirring.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Maud's grip doesn't loosen and neither does her voice, and it's that steadiness — not threat — that finally does it: Yara Breaks, the words tumbling out of her in a rush like she's been drowning under them for weeks. "The Priest," she sobs, "the Drowned Priest's people came to me at the quarantine fence, said the swarm has a rhythm, said if I listened and counted it back I'd never get sick, never get taken — I just had to listen, that's all, I just had to count—" Fenwick, crouched at her other side, goes very still as the numbers she's been chanting click into place against something he already knows: the cadence matches Bren's old survey-notation, the private shorthand only the two of them ever used out in the reeds. Whoever taught Yara this rhythm either found Bren's notes or found Bren. Above them the quarantine bells keep tolling, insistent now, and Hask — Positioned to Intercept at the foot of the stairs — hears the boots slow at the top, someone listening back down into the dark. Eira, folded into the shadow at the bottom step where light doesn't reach, is close enough to touch whoever comes down first, and it won't be a fair fight for them. But the bells mean this cellar isn't a secret anymore, not to the Wardens and maybe not to the cartel either — whatever the party does next, it has to be fast.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Rell was a water-seller's daughter from Hollowmoot's market—I took her under my wing and tried to teach her the ferry ways, even though my family said her blood wasn't right for it. I swore she could belong if she tried hard enough. She thinks I'd forgive her because I always did, no matter what. I chose to believe in her when no one else would.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Rell? No—I freeze, her name hitting me like a rigged current, and instead of shouting warning my eyes snap to the enforcers' faces, hunting for ferry-family blood among them, certain she couldn't have done this alone, that someone with real family had to be involved.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Hask accepts the compel on 'Born on the Ferry Lines'.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: I swore to Bren in the old way—hand over heart—that I would never hand over the channels leading to the Holdfast Deep. When the swarm came for him, he made me promise because those maps are the only path to sanctuary where the hive-touched can heal, where the desperate can hide. If they fall into the wrong hands, everyone sheltering there dies.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: I can't, Rell. I swore to Bren in blood, and I won't break that oath—not even for a home.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Fenwick refuses the compel on 'Cast Out from the Stilt Villages'.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: I know what Tallow's money buys, and I know what I owe—but not tonight. You tell the Cartel they can collect their favor some other time, because if they want those enforcers steered anywhere, they'll have to come down here and do it themselves.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira accepts the compel on 'The Cartels Ledger'.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: The betrayer is Rell, a cousin from Hask's own ferry-line family — someone who poled boats beside him as a child and knows the Gullet Ford as well as he does. turns on the party, because The cartel's people cornered Rell and squeezed: they want Fenwick's forbidden knowledge of every hidden channel between Hollowmoot and the reeds, and Rell's price for keeping her own family dry was to lead the enforcers straight to the party..

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The hatch groans open above black water and lantern-light spills down with it — and there, leading two hard-eyed enforcers with hooked cargo-spears, is a face Hask would know anywhere, dripping and pale and refusing to meet his eyes. "Rell," he says, and the name comes out wrong, like a rope giving way. She doesn't answer him. She looks past him, straight at Fenwick, at the satchel of maps he's never let out of arm's reach. "The channels to the Holdfast," she says, voice flat, rehearsed. "That's all they want. Give it over and nobody in this cellar has to bleed for it." Behind her the enforcers spread to block both the hatch and the stair, and Yara, still shaking in Maud's arms, goes rigid with fresh terror at the sight of them.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: You know what happens when I hold the line, Rell. Not tonight. Not for the Cartel.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud plants her feet solid, one hand steadying Yara behind her, the other settling calm on her blade-hilt. She looks straight at Rell—waiting to see if betrayal runs deep enough to cross the line she's drawn.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Rell, I know the Cartel squeezed you dry to get you here—I can read water in your face same as I can read current, and I know the price they'd demand. But those maps go nowhere, and neither do you past me. Not while Fenwick stands behind me and Yara stops shaking.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask steps forward into the center of the low chamber, his boots finding purchase on the wet stone as he plants himself between Rell and the others—between the enforcers and Fenwick, between them and Yara still shaking in Maud's arms. His hand moves to his pole-knife almost absently, though he doesn't draw it yet. His eyes stay fixed on Rell's face, searching for the girl he taught the ferry-ways to, even knowing what she's just done.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: Move, or I'll move you myself.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira steps forward into the enforcer's reach without hesitation, using her intimate knowledge of Wick Lane's cellars to move through their spacing—these passages are her ground, every water-slick stone and low arch as familiar as the dark she's worked births in a hundred times over. She comes at the lead enforcer directly, compact and brutal, not asking for passage but making it clear she'll carve one out.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: I swore an oath to Bren in blood—that oath doesn't break for Cartel steel or for you, Rell.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick's hand doesn't loosen on the map-satchel. He shifts his weight back toward the water, not fleeing but claiming the ground where he knows every hidden passage, every escape route. His eyes track both enforcers' positions with the precision of someone measuring a map—assessing angles, exits, the channels that run beneath this cellar like veins through stone.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira — attack with Athletics: dice 0 + + +, invoking Knows the Wick Lane Cellars hidden paths [EI-04] → Fantastic (+6) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS WITH STYLE (Cartel Enforcer (lead) mild consequence)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Cartel Enforcer (second) attacks Fenwick (physical): Average (+1) vs Fenwick's Athletics Mediocre (+0) — hit for 1

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Rell attacks Hask (mental): Great (+4) vs Hask's Will Terrible (-2) — hit for 6

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Eira doesn't just get past the lead enforcer — she uses the cellar itself against him, ducking a spear-thrust into a gap only someone who's crawled these tunnels a hundred times would know was there, and puts him down gasping against the brick with his own weapon skidding into the black water. The second enforcer's hook catches Fenwick's satchel strap and nearly has it, but Fenwick twists with the pull instead of against it, taking the wrench on his shoulder instead of losing the maps — the channels to the Holdfast stay slung across his back, and his eyes never leave the enforcer's feet, still cataloguing the room like a map he means to escape by. But it's Rell's words that do the real damage. She doesn't come at Hask with steel — she comes at him with the truth of every kindness he ever showed her, twisting it into a blade: "I'm saving myself, Hask, the way you taught me." It lands exactly where she aimed it. Hask doesn't flinch from a blow he can see coming; he flinches from one he can't, and for a moment the ferryman who reads any current goes still, rocked all the way down, Rell's betrayal ringing through him hard enough to leave him doubting his own judgment in the middle of a fight he still has to win.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: You want what he carries? You come through me first.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud steadies Yara with one final grounding touch, then steps forward to place herself directly between Fenwick and the second enforcer. Her blade slides free with the practiced certainty of a militia guard, and she meets him head-on with the unflinching resolve of someone who knows how to hold a line when everything else is breaking.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: The maps don't go anywhere through me.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Despite Rell's words still ringing in my skull, I step forward into the enforcer's reach. My pole-knife comes up fast and low, trying to slash at their spear-arm and break their grip on Fenwick's satchel—anything to force them to drop their weapon or pull back from the maps.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: Work for the Cartel? Fine. But not here. Not in my ground.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira moves like these cellars are part of her body—three quick strides through gaps only she knows exist, through shadows the lantern can't quite reach. She comes at Rell without warning, closing distance with predatory speed, and gets a solid grip before Rell can even flinch. The hatch-water is right behind her now.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: This way. Trust the water.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick's eyes find the seams in the stone with the precision of long study—these passages live in his fingertips. There's a channel beneath this cellar, running dark and deep to places only he knows. He turns toward the water's edge, satchel held close, hand reaching back to anyone who will follow. The enforcers brought steel and spears. He brought something better: maps of every drowned road between here and sanctuary.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Maud — attack with Fight: dice + 0 0 0, invoking Never breaks a shield-wall [MA-03] → Fantastic (+6) vs Great (+4): SUCCESS (Cartel Enforcer (second) stress 2)

transcript.speaker: Table

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira — attack with Athletics: dice + + + + → Superb (+5) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS (Rell stress 2)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Fenwick — create advantage with Lore: dice 0 + 0 0 → Superb (+5) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The second enforcer folds first, Hask's slash across his spear-arm and Maud's blade at his throat together finishing what stubbornness started — he drops the hook and puts his hands up against the wet stone, done fighting for cartel coin. Eira doesn't let go of Rell; she drags her back from the hatch-water hard enough to rattle her teeth, close enough to hiss "not here, not on my ground" right into her ear. Rell struggles once, twice, then goes slack, Stress 2 finally outweighing whatever the cartel promised her family. And Fenwick's find pays off exactly when it's needed — the seam in the stone he traced opens onto a drowned channel that runs clean under Wick Lane and out past the Warden bells now tolling somewhere far above, a way out that doesn't pass a single enforcer or a single set of Warden eyes. Hask keeps his knife low and his voice lower as he looks at his cousin one last time — no words this time, just the current reading her face and finding nothing left worth trusting. They go, Yara pulled gently along by Maud, the maps to the Holdfast still slung across Fenwick's back, into water that swallows the sound of bells and betrayal both.
